newsitem.title: UK: OECD expects further small UK rate rise.
newsitem.headline: OECD expects further small UK rate rise.

text.p: The Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) said it expected a further small rise in UK base rates in the second half of 1997.

In its twice-yearly report, which was prepared before last week's quarter-point rise in UK base rates to 6.5 percent from 6.25, it said short-term prospects for inflation were favourable due to sterling's strong appreciation since mid-1996 and the first quarter-point rate rise in May.
"A further small rise is assumed in base rates in the second half of 1997 to contain rising cost pressures as the damping effects of sterling appreciation fade," the OECD said.
Prospects for sustained output growth with low inflation remained favourable, the OECD said.

"But the outlook would be more balanced had original plans for fiscal consolidation been realised -- thereby easing subsequent upward pressure on sterling (and long-term interest rates) and favouring a recovery more conducive to higher investment levels and a more competitive tradeable sector."
The OECD estimated GDP growth at 3.0 percent during 1997, slowing progressively through 1998 towards 2-1/2 percent.
"Private consumption growth is projected to be sustained by stronger job creation and improving household balance-sheet positions."
The OECD said the output gap would be eliminated by the end of 1998 and the unemployment rate would be close to its estimated structural rate.
"Near-term cost pressures will be damped by falling import costs but tightening labour markets could see some further pickup in wage growth," it said.
"Inflation could drop to two percent in 1997 but once the effects of lower import prices fade, modest inflation pressures could re-emerge."
